reflection.text:
Unblinded truth was floxuridine, a thymidylate synthase inhibitor in the DNA replication class, while I concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors at p=0.50. The phenotype I measured - dose-dependent cell enlargement with cell_area z +5.8 to +14.1 and rho=+1.00, lower density, and large nuclei - is consistent in retrospect with unbalanced growth from replication stress (PMID 1532343, PMID 6450011), not specific to Aurora.

I was misled by the early compare_to_reference_atlas NSC vote 2/2 for Aurora (e4) and microscopist agreement for Aurora (e5), then retained that prior even after it decayed to 2/4 with very low similarities 0.17-0.26 and split neighbours 5/10 Aurora vs 4/10 Protein degradation and votes for DNA damage and Cholesterol-lowering (e8 and verdict protocol). I misread e2 frac_large_nucleus z=+17.5 and cell_area enlargement as polyploidy-like Aurora signal while discounting e11 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.11 non-monotone, e10 nuc_area rho=+0.40 p=0.6 flat, e12 tub_mean flat, and e13 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.63 p=0.37 non-significant which argued against a mitotic-failure mechanism.

The error was compounded by acquisition choices: only 4 wells all rep1 at 0.3, 3, 10, 30 uM with no replicates and no S-phase or DNA-damage readout, so a single noisy 3 uM well drove the large-nucleus signal and the low-dose 0.3 uM well voting DNA damage was down-weighted instead of prompting an EdU/DNA-content test.
what_was_right: Correctly quantified a real dose-dependent enlarged-cell phenotype: cell_area z +5.8 at 0.3uM to +14.1 at 30uM with rho=+1.00 (e2,e3,e6,e7,e9) and lower density (e5).
Correctly used flat tub_mean dose response (e12 rho=-0.80 p=0.2) and flat/non-significant frac_mitotic_like (e13) to down-weight microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer and Eg5 hypotheses (e14).
Kept DNA damage in the hypothesis set (0.10 in e14) because k-neighbours included DNA damage and the low-dose well voted DNA damage, which was the closest to the true replication-stress biology.
what_was_wrong: Overweighted weak NSC similarity: treated 2/2 then 2/4 Aurora votes with similarities 0.258, 0.233 falling to 0.17-0.26 as a prior for Aurora despite split tally and runner-up Protein degradation 4/10 neighbours (e4,e8,verdict).

Misinterpreted enlarged cells + e2 frac_large_nucleus z=+17.5 as Aurora polyploidy while ignoring e11 non-monotone frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.11 p=0.89 and e10 nuc_area not tracking cell_area, plus lack of mitotic accumulation in e13.

Gave decisive weight to microscopist sole-candidate Aurora call (e5) and discounted the low-dose w_62dd17d7bc DNA-damage nearest neighbour and the 10uM Cholesterol-lowering vote as noise rather than evidence of low atlas specificity.

Acquired only 4 wells all rep1 with no replicate wells and no replication-stress measurement, so single-well z-scores and a 4-point dose response could not distinguish S-phase arrest/unbalanced growth from Aurora cytokinesis failure.

Resistance to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine involves regulation of thymidylate synthase enzyme synthesis.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top MoA favoured: 1-NN atlas 2/4 were Aurora vs 0 for runner-up, 5/10 vs 4/10 neighbours (sim 0.17-0.26), microscopist independently sole candidate Aurora. 4-dose cell/nuc enlargement (cell_area z 5.8→14.1, rho=1.0; nuc_area z 3.9-5.0 at ≥3µM) with flat tubulin/mitotic fraction argues against microtubule/Eg5. ## Unblinding

Compound: **floxuridine** (PubChem CID [5790](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5790))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Thymidylate synthase inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth was floxuridine, a thymidylate synthase inhibitor in the DNA replication class, while I concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors at p=0.50. The phenotype I measured - dose-dependent cell enlargement with cell_area z +5.8 to +14.1 and rho=+1.00, lower density, and large nuclei - is consistent in retrospect with unbalanced growth from replication stress (PMID 1532343, PMID 6450011), not specific to Aurora.

I was misled by the early compare_to_reference_atlas NSC vote 2/2 for Aurora (e4) and microscopist agreement for Aurora (e5), then retained that prior even after it decayed to 2/4 with very low similarities 0.17-0.26 and split neighbours 5/10 Aurora vs 4/10 Protein degradation and votes for DNA damage and Cholesterol-lowering (e8 and verdict protocol). I misread e2 frac_large_nucleus z=+17.5 and cell_area enlargement as polyploidy-like Aurora signal while discounting e11 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.11 non-monotone, e10 nuc_area rho=+0.40 p=0.6 flat, e12 tub_mean flat, and e13 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.63 p=0.37 non-significant which argued against a mitotic-failure mechanism.

The error was compounded by acquisition choices: only 4 wells all rep1 at 0.3, 3, 10, 30 uM with no replicates and no S-phase or DNA-damage readout, so a single noisy 3 uM well drove the large-nucleus signal and the low-dose 0.3 uM well voting DNA damage was down-weighted instead of prompting an EdU/DNA-content test.

What was right:
- Correctly quantified a real dose-dependent enlarged-cell phenotype: cell_area z +5.8 at 0.3uM to +14.1 at 30uM with rho=+1.00 (e2,e3,e6,e7,e9) and lower density (e5).
- Correctly used flat tub_mean dose response (e12 rho=-0.80 p=0.2) and flat/non-significant frac_mitotic_like (e13) to down-weight microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer and Eg5 hypotheses (e14).
- Kept DNA damage in the hypothesis set (0.10 in e14) because k-neighbours included DNA damage and the low-dose well voted DNA damage, which was the closest to the true replication-stress biology.

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted weak NSC similarity: treated 2/2 then 2/4 Aurora votes with similarities 0.258, 0.233 falling to 0.17-0.26 as a prior for Aurora despite split tally and runner-up Protein degradation 4/10 neighbours (e4,e8,verdict).
- Misinterpreted enlarged cells + e2 frac_large_nucleus z=+17.5 as Aurora polyploidy while ignoring e11 non-monotone frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.11 p=0.89 and e10 nuc_area not tracking cell_area, plus lack of mitotic accumulation in e13.
- Gave decisive weight to microscopist sole-candidate Aurora call (e5) and discounted the low-dose w_62dd17d7bc DNA-damage nearest neighbour and the 10uM Cholesterol-lowering vote as noise rather than evidence of low atlas specificity.
- Acquired only 4 wells all rep1 with no replicate wells and no replication-stress measurement, so single-well z-scores and a 4-point dose response could not distinguish S-phase arrest/unbalanced growth from Aurora cytokinesis failure.

Proposed next experiment: Pulse-label with EdU plus DNA-content flow cytometry and co-stain for phospho-histone H3 (mitotic/Aurora activity) versus phospho-H2AX/p53-p21 (replication stress/DNA damage) across 0.3-30 uM floxuridine with time-lapse to test S-phase arrest and unbalanced enlargement versus cytokinesis failure and polyploidy.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [1532343](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1532343/): Radiosensitization by fluorodeoxyuridine: effects of thymidylate synthase inhibition and cell synchronization. *Cancer Res* (1992) — Fluorodeoxyuridine causes radiosensitization through thymidylate synthase inhibition and effects on cell synchronization.
- PMID [3155521](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3155521/): Regulation of thymidylate synthase enzyme synthesis in 5-fluorodeoxyuridine-resistant mouse fibroblasts during the transition from the resting to growing state. *J Cell Physiol* (1985) — Resistance to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine involves regulation of thymidylate synthase enzyme synthesis.
- PMID [6450011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6450011/): Drug-induced megaloblastic change. *Clin Haematol* (1980) — Drugs that interfere with DNA synthesis can produce megaloblastic change with enlarged cells and nuclei.
